standard.title: Share arts works with audiences
standard.description: share their arts works with audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have no formal sharing or presenting experience assumed. They bring familiarity with informal show-and-tell and play-based sharing with peers.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share artworks with an audience and explain something about the work — its ideas, processes or features.

nodes.label: What audiences do
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify what it means to be an audience — that others look at, listen to or watch arts works, and that the audience receives something from the work.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate as an audience member for a peer's work; share one thing noticed or felt.
nodes.typical_width: Participate as audience and maker in informal sharing contexts; identify features of artworks when looking at peers' work (similarities, differences, use of materials, visual elements).
wider: Walk around a class gallery and use positive language to comment on specific features of peers' works (line, colour, shape, materials)
Watch a performance or sharing of a different arts form — describe what the audience does and what the experience is like
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have no concept of an audience share work without communicative intent — they cannot make meaningful choices about how to present or explain their work.

response_modes.reason: The audience role needs to be experienced from both sides — as receiver and as presenter. Students who have only made, without experiencing what it is to receive, lack the perspective needed for intentional sharing.

success_criteria: Participates as an audience member for a peer's work
Shares at least one observation about the work

nodes.label: Sharing with explanation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share an artwork with an audience and say something about it — what it shows, what they used to make it, or what they enjoyed.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one artwork and say one thing about it — what it shows, what it is made from, or what was enjoyable about making it.
nodes.typical_width: Share artworks in multiple informal settings; talk about ideas, processes, materials and features; respond to teacher questions; present to small groups and to the class.
wider: Use a digital device to document an artwork or making process — curate a short sequence of images with added commentary expressing feelings and understandings
Present a retelling of a story using objects, puppets or repurposed materials — respond to audience questions about the story and the choices made

response_modes.reason: Sharing becomes more intentional when students experience multiple contexts (gallery walk, one-to-one with teacher, group presentation) — each context demands slightly different communication and builds versatility.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital documentation, object-based retelling and gallery-walk formats each offer distinct sharing contexts that build different aspects of communicative presentation — all genuinely accessible at Foundation.
success_criteria: Shares at least one artwork with an audience
Says at least one thing about the work — what it shows, what it is made from, or what was enjoyable
